Definition: from G1909 and a reduplicated derivative of the base of G939 (compare G307); to cause to mount (an animal):--set on.
BiblicalUsage: Epibibazo means to set upon — to set a man on a beast. The Samaritan sets the wounded man on his own beast and brings him to an inn; the disciples set Jesus on the colt; the soldiers are ordered to provide beasts to set Paul on, to bring him safe to Felix.
TheologicalSignificance: Somebody else's beast, somebody else's trouble, carried at somebody else's cost — that is the gospel in miniature. I believe the Samaritan, the disciples, and the soldiers each set a man on a beast, and each time the carrying pictures Christ carrying me.
